title: Vegetable bulgur
method: Dice the carrot and the parsley root or parsnip, and chop the tomato.
Simmer the vegetables in the water until very soft, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the bulgur and the peas and cook until the bulgur is soft and the liquid is absorbed.
Crush the peas, then stir in the olive oil.
Mash the serving for a baby who is not yet chewing, and check that every piece squashes.
issues: This grain pot is often held back until 9 or 10 months, and it is sometimes cooked in salty stock. Whole peas are also awkward if a baby is only just starting to chew.
changes: Cook the bulgur and vegetables in plain water until they squash easily, and crush the peas. Offer it from 8 months, and mash the serving for a baby who is not chewing yet.
serve: Offer it warm and soft enough to squash. Mash it for a baby who is not chewing yet.

title: Green pasta with cheese

ingredients.note: dry weight, cooked until very soft

method: Boil the pasta in unsalted water until very soft, then drain it.
Cook the garlic in the olive oil for under a minute without browning it hard.
Add the broccoli and spinach with a splash of water and cook until they mash easily.
Chop or mash the greens and toss them through the pasta.
Stir in the yogurt and the cheese off the heat, and do not add salt.
issues: The usual plate was salted and very rich with a cup of cream, and it was often served around 11 months. A pinch of salt and that much cream are unnecessary for a baby.
changes: Use soft pasta with spinach, broccoli, and a little garlic cooked in olive oil. Stir in one spoon of plain yogurt and a little pasteurized cheese, and add no salt.
serve: Cut or mash any piece that does not squash, and serve warm rather than hot. Stir the yogurt in just before eating.

title: Tomato chicken pasta
method: Cook the chicken and garlic in the oil until the meat is opaque all the way through.
Add the tomato and water and simmer until the chicken is very soft and the sauce thickens.
Boil the pasta in unsalted water until soft, then drain it.
Stir in the basil or parsley, and do not add salt or black pepper.
Chop or mash the chicken and pasta to the texture the baby can manage.
issues: The usual tomato chicken pasta was salted and seasoned with black pepper, often at 9 or 10 months. Pepper is harsh here, and the pasta and chicken need to be soft enough to squash.
changes: Leave out the salt and the black pepper, and use basil or parsley instead. Keep the chicken and pasta very soft, and chop or mash the portion.
serve: Offer soft chopped pieces or a mash. Check the chicken for gristle before serving.

title: Baby bolognese
method: Soften the onion in the oil, then add the mince and cook until no pink remains.
Stir in the carrot, zucchini, tomato, and water, and do not add a stock cube.
Simmer until the vegetables are soft and the sauce is thick, about 20 minutes.
Boil the pasta in unsalted water until very soft, then drain it.
Chop or mash the sauce with the pasta, and cool extra portions quickly.
issues: This is a sound idea once the salt is gone, but the usual sauce is made with a salted stock cube. That salt is the problem, not the beef, vegetables, or soft pasta.
changes: Simmer the mince and vegetables in unsalted tomato and water, with no stock cube. Mash or chop the pasta and sauce for the baby, and freeze the extra.
serve: Serve a small mashed or finely chopped bowl. Freeze extra sauce in small pots and thaw it in the fridge.

title: Vegetable shepherd's pie

ingredients.note: half for the filling, half for the mash

method: Soften the onion in the oil, then add the carrot, green beans, half the cauliflower, the peas, and the water.
Cook until the beans and cauliflower are completely soft, then crush the peas, and add no salt.
Boil the potato and the remaining cauliflower until tender, then mash them with the milk.
Stir the egg yolk and the tablespoon of cheese into the mash, and add no nutmeg.
Spread the mash over the ragout and bake at 190 C until the topping is hot and the yolk is fully set, about 20 minutes.
Cool slightly and offer soft spoonfuls, mashed if the baby is not chewing yet.
issues: The usual pie was salted, and nutmeg is often added to the potato topping. Green beans also stay fibrous if they are undercooked.
changes: Bake an unsalted vegetable ragout under a potato and cauliflower mash bound with a little milk and one egg yolk, with no nutmeg. Cook the beans until soft, and keep the cheese to one tablespoon.
serve: Spoon out a soft portion and mash it if the baby is not chewing well yet. The beans should crush, not stay firm.

title: Mild paprika stew

ingredients.note: pasteurized, stirred in off the heat

method: Soften the onion in the oil, then stir in the paprika.
Add the chicken or rabbit, carrot, parsnip, and sweet potato.
Pour in the water and simmer until the meat and vegetables are very soft, with no mustard, vinegar, or bay leaf.
Shred the meat and check it for bone or gristle.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the yogurt, and mash or chop the stew.
issues: The usual stew used mustard, vinegar, and sour cream. Mustard is harsh and salty for this age, and vinegar is too sharp.
changes: Mustard was dropped. This version is a mild paprika stew of carrot, parsnip, sweet potato, onion, and chicken or rabbit, with the bay leaf left out and plain yogurt stirred in at the end.
serve: Mash the stew or offer soft pieces. Freeze it without the yogurt, then stir the yogurt in after reheating and cooling.

title: Fish with broccoli and kohlrabi
method: Peel and finely dice the kohlrabi, then cook it in the water until a piece crushes easily.
Add the broccoli and cook until it is soft.
Lay the fish in the pan and poach it until it flakes, then check every flake and remove any bone.
Boil the pasta in unsalted water until very soft, then drain it.
Toss the fish, vegetables, pasta, cheese, and oil, and mash any piece that does not squash.
issues: Kohlrabi is fibrous if it is undercooked, and any missed bone makes the fish unsafe. A large amount of cheese would also be too salty.
changes: Cook boneless fish, broccoli, and kohlrabi until very soft, and check the flakes for bones. Use only a little pasteurized cheese with small pasta, and mash anything the baby cannot chew.
serve: Flake the fish and mash any firm piece. Kohlrabi should crush completely before it is served.

title: Green salmon with rice

ingredients.note: for boiling the rice and vegetables

method: Boil the rice in plenty of unsalted water until soft, then drain it and spread it to cool quickly.
Simmer the broccoli until it mashes, and wilt the spinach in the same pan.
Poach the salmon until it flakes, then check the flakes and remove any bone.
Stir the rice, vegetables, and salmon together and break up any firm piece.
Stir in the olive oil.
issues: This plate is already suitable at 8 months when the salmon is boneless and the rice and vegetables are soft. A missed bone, or rice left sitting warm, is the hazard to manage.
changes: No reformulation is needed. Check the salmon for bones, stir in a teaspoon of olive oil at the end, and cool the rice quickly.
serve: Serve soft and warm after a final bone check. Refrigerate rice and eat it within a day.

title: Fish baked in paper

ingredients.item: boneless salmon, trout, cod, or hake

ingredients.note: white part only, well washed and sliced

method: Lay the fillet on baking paper with the leek, fresh tomato, and zucchini.
Drizzle with the oil, fold a parcel, and bake at 180 C until the fish flakes and the vegetables are soft, about 20 minutes.
Open the parcel, flake the fish, and check every flake for bones.
Mash the fish and vegetables together until smooth enough for 6 months.
issues: The usual parcel was often carp, sometimes with salty dried tomato, and Brussels sprouts do not cook down to a mash here. At 6 months the fish cannot be left in large flakes.
changes: Bake a boneless salmon, trout, cod, or hake fillet with leek, fresh tomato, and zucchini, not carp or dried tomato. Flake it, check for bones, and mash it with the vegetables.
serve: Mash until smooth enough for 6 months, with no bone and no firm vegetable lumps. Offer a small spoonful while it is warm.

title: Oven fish fingers

ingredients.note: beaten, cooked through in the oven

method: Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a sheet of baking paper.
Cut the fish into squat strips, not coins, and check for bones.
Dip each strip in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Bake until the fish is opaque and the coating is pale and soft, not hard and not fried.
Cool until warm and check that the strip squashes and the egg is fully set.
issues: Fried fish fingers turn hard at the crust, and coin-shaped pieces are awkward to hold. A crust is harder to manage before 9 months.
changes: Coat boneless cod or hake in flour, egg, and fine breadcrumbs, then bake it on paper until the coating is soft, not fried. Cut squat strips rather than coins.
serve: Give squat strips once the coating is cool enough to hold. The outside should yield, not crack.

title: Beef meatballs
method: Heat the oven to 190 C.
Squeeze the grated zucchini or carrot dry and mix it with the mince, egg, oats or breadcrumbs, and parsley.
Add no salt and no nutmeg, and roll small balls about 2 cm across.
Bake on a lightly oiled tray until the centers are cooked through and still soft, about 18 minutes, and do not fry them.
Cool one and squash it to check that it is soft enough to gum.
issues: Meatballs are often fried hard and seasoned with salt and nutmeg. A browned crust is too firm, and large balls are hard to gum.
changes: Bind beef or pork mince with squeezed grated zucchini or carrot, egg, oats or breadcrumbs, and parsley. Bake small balls until soft all the way through, with no salt and no nutmeg.
serve: Offer small soft balls, or cut one open to show it is cooked through. Squash a piece if the baby is still new to chewing.

title: Chicken nuggets
method: Heat the oven to 190 C.
Mix the chicken, celeriac, parsley, egg, and breadcrumbs, and add no salt.
Shape small flat nuggets on a lightly oiled tray.
Bake until the center is white and soft, about 18 minutes, and do not deep-fry them.
Cool and squash any piece that feels firm.
issues: Typical nuggets are deep-fried until the outside is hard. Celeriac, used here for flavor, is a celery allergen.
changes: Bake minced chicken with grated celeriac, herbs, egg, and breadcrumbs until the inside is soft. Do not deep-fry them, and add no salt.
serve: Serve warm nuggets that squash easily. The celeriac means this plate contains celery.

title: Lentil and carrot bites

ingredients.note: pasteurized and finely grated, not cheddar

method: Simmer the lentils, carrot, and sweet potato in the water until very soft and the lentils have collapsed.
Drain any extra liquid and mash until almost smooth.
Stir in the egg, the mild cheese, and the coriander if you want it, and do not use cheddar.
Shape small flat bites and bake at 190 C until the egg is set and the outside is still soft.
Do not fry them, then cool and squash one to check the texture.
issues: Cheddar is very salty for this age, and frying would put a hard crust on an iron-rich bite. The lentils and vegetables have to be fully soft before they are shaped.
changes: Cook red lentils, carrot, and sweet potato until soft, then bind them with egg and a small amount of mild pasteurized cheese, or skip the cheese. Bake the bites instead of frying them, and add coriander only if you want it.
serve: These are a useful iron-rich food. Serve soft bites warm.

title: Vegetable nuggets

ingredients.note: cooked weight, fully boiled, or unsalted canned and rinsed

method: Cook the broccoli and carrot until very soft, and use white beans that have been boiled until completely soft.
Mash the vegetables and beans so no whole beans remain.
Stir in the egg and oats, and add no salt.
Shape small nuggets and bake at 190 C on oiled paper until just set, with a soft outside rather than a hard crust.
Cool and check that a nugget squashes easily.
issues: These nuggets are often salted and cooked until the oat coating turns hard. White beans are not safe for a baby unless they are fully boiled.
changes: Mash broccoli, carrot, and fully boiled white beans with egg and oats, and bake them only until just set. Keep the outside soft and add no salt.
serve: Offer soft nuggets that squash between your fingers. Do not serve any whole beans.

title: Vegetable patties
method: Cook the broccoli, carrot, and peas until very soft, then chop them and crush the peas.
Mix in the mince, cheese, and garlic, and add no salt and no pepper.
Shape small flat patties. No egg is needed.
Bake at 190 C, or cook in a thin film of oil over moderate heat, until the meat is cooked through and the outside stays soft.
Do not brown them hard, then cool slightly and cut into soft strips or mash.
issues: The usual patties were salted and peppered, then browned until the outside was firm. That crust is harder than an 8-month-old needs.
changes: Mix broccoli, carrot, pea, and chicken or rabbit mince with a little cheese and garlic, with no salt and no pepper. Bake the patties, or cook them in a thin film of oil over moderate heat, until they stay soft rather than browned hard.
serve: Serve soft strips or a mashed spoonful. Peas should be crushed, not left whole and firm.

title: Chickpea patties

ingredients.note: dried chickpeas boiled until soft, or unsalted canned, rinsed
finely chopped and cooked until soft

method: Start with chickpeas boiled until completely soft, or use rinsed unsalted canned chickpeas.
Mash them with the cooked onion, garlic, and parsley, leaving only a few soft lumps.
Stir in the egg and oats, and add no salt.
Shape small patties and bake at 190 C on an oiled tray until the egg is set and the patties stay soft.
Cool and squash one before serving.
issues: Dried chickpeas stay hard and difficult to mash if they are not fully boiled, and the usual patties are salted. A dark fried crust is also too tough at 8 months.
changes: Use chickpeas boiled until soft, or rinsed unsalted canned chickpeas. Bind them with onion, garlic, herbs, egg, and oats, then bake them with no salt.
serve: Offer soft patties, broken up if needed. Every chickpea piece should mash, with no hard centers.

title: Chickpea pancakes

ingredients.note: finely chopped and cooked until soft

method: Cook the onion and sweet pepper until soft.
Mix the chickpea flour, water, and turmeric, then stir in the carrot, onion, and sweet pepper.
Add no salt and no curry powder.
Oil a pan lightly and cook small pancakes over moderate heat until the underside is set, then turn them.
Cook until the center is fully set, then cool and cut into soft strips.
issues: The usual seasoning is a salty curry powder, and an undercooked pancake stays wet in the middle. Chickpea is not peanut, so it is not listed as a peanut allergen.
changes: Cook chickpea-flour pancakes with grated carrot, cooked onion, and sweet pepper, and season them with turmeric rather than curry powder. Cook the batter through and add no salt.
serve: Cut into soft strips. The center of each pancake should be dry and fully cooked.

title: Vegetable fritters

ingredients.note: use rice for a gluten-free fritter

method: Mash the corn so no whole kernels remain.
Mix the eggs with the grated carrot, mashed corn, and cooked bulgur.
Use soft cooked rice instead of bulgur in that step if the fritter must be gluten-free.
Heat a thin film of oil and cook small fritters over moderate heat, then turn them.
Cook until the egg is fully set and the fritter is soft rather than crisp, and add no salt.
issues: Whole corn kernels are a choking hazard, and the usual note already warned them off for younger babies. Salt is also unnecessary in this egg batter.
changes: Mash the corn before it goes into the batter. Pan-fry egg with grated carrot and cooked bulgur, or use cooked rice in that step when you need a gluten-free fritter, and add no salt.
serve: Serve soft pieces, never loose corn kernels. Use the rice version when the meal must be free of gluten.

title: Soft vegetable flatbread

ingredients.note: 1 tsp in the dough and 1 tsp on the vegetables
simmered to a thick sauce with no salt
diced small and roasted until soft
diced small and roasted until soft
diced small and roasted until soft

method: Mix the flour, yeast, water, and 1 tsp of oil into a soft dough, and add no sugar and no salt.
Knead briefly, cover the dough, and leave it until puffy, about 45 minutes.
Roast the zucchini, sweet pepper, and onion until soft while the dough rises, and simmer the tomato into a thick sauce.
Press the dough into a small tray so it stays thin, then spread on the tomato, vegetables, and mozzarella.
Bake at 200 C until the base is cooked but still soft and the cheese has melted, about 12 minutes, and do not add ham.
Cool and cut into squares.
issues: The usual mini pizza used ham, cane sugar, and salt, and it was aimed at 9 or 10 months. Ham is a salty cured meat, and at that age the bread is too chewy.
changes: Ham and sugar were the problem, and the bread texture is why it waits until 12 months. Bake a soft yeast flatbread with no sugar and no salt, top it with tomato, roasted vegetables, and a little mozzarella, and cut it into squares.
serve: Cut into squares and serve warm as soft pieces. The base should bend, not shatter.

title: Banana pancakes
method: Mash the banana until smooth.
Beat in the egg and the flour, and add no sugar.
Heat a thin film of oil on low heat.
Cook small pancakes until the underside is set, then turn them.
Cook until the egg is fully set in the center, then mash or break them for the baby.
issues: Ripe banana, egg, and a little flour are already a plain batter, with no need for sugar. The pancake is a problem only if the center stays raw or the round is too thick to mash.
changes: No ingredient change is needed. Cook small pancakes in a thin film of oil on low heat until the egg is fully set, and do not add sugar.
serve: Break into mashable pieces or mash the serving for a 6-month-old. Leave them unsweetened.

title: Apple and curd pancakes

ingredients.note: pasteurized, preferably with no added salt

method: Grate the apple and cook it with a splash of water until soft, then mash it.
Mix in the egg, cottage cheese, oats, and flour, and add no sugar and no salt.
Cook small pancakes in a thin film of oil over low heat.
Turn them and cook until the egg is fully set and the center is not wet.
Cool and mash or break them for a 6-month-old.
issues: Cooked apple, egg, pasteurized cottage cheese, oats, and a spoon of flour are already suitable at 6 months when the pancake is soft and fully set. The apple has to be grated and cooked so it mashes, and the cheese has to be pasteurized.
changes: No salt or sugar is added. Cook the pancakes through, then mash or break them for a baby who is still gumming food.
serve: Mash or break into very soft pieces. Use only pasteurized cottage cheese.
